1. In 1950, the total strength, including the Chief Justice of India, was 8.
2. In 2008, the total strength, including the Chief Justice of India, was 34.
3. In 2026, the proposed total strength, including the Chief Justice of India, is 38.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
1.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: the total strength was 8 in 1950 and is proposed to be 38 in 2026. Statement 2 is incorrect because the total strength in 2008 was 31, not 34.
1.tq: Multi-Statement Correctness · tests the “Evolution of Supreme Court strength” angle
n: Year: 1950; Total: 8 [May 2026 · Supreme Court strength raised to 38]
Year: 2008; Total: 31 [May 2026 · Supreme Court strength raised to 38]
Year: 2026 (proposed); Total: 38 [May 2026 · Supreme Court strength raised to 38]

n: Constituted by: MHA — study demographic changes from illegal immigration and other abnormal reasons [May 2026 · High-Level Committee on demographic change]

Reason (R): The Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act was enacted in 1882.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A

o: The Allahabad High Court upheld the District Level Committee’s rejection of Tharu tribe claims.

The doctrine lex posterior derogat priori means that a later law overrides an earlier law.

1.x: The incorrect statement is the second one. The Allahabad High Court set aside, rather than upheld, the District Level Committee’s rejection of Tharu tribe claims; the other statements correctly describe the rulings and the Forest Rights Act position.

1.s: According to the Supreme Court ruling concerning the inclusion of Rajasthani in a teacher recruitment examination syllabus, what was recognised as part of the right to identity?
o: Thinking and expressing in one’s own language
Only instruction in a mother tongue at the primary stage
Only the preference for mother tongue under NEP 2020
Inclusion of every regional language in every teacher recruitment examination
1.x: The Supreme Court recognised that thinking and expressing in one’s language forms part of the right to identity. Article 350A concerns instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage for linguistic minority children, while NEP 2020 favours mother tongue; neither creates the broader claim in the other options.
1.tq: Direct Recall · tests the “Mother tongue and fundamental right” angle

1.s: What change did the Supreme Court make in Hamsanandini Nanduri v. Union of India regarding maternity leave for adoptive mothers?
o: Adoptive mothers are entitled to leave only after verification by the Authority
Only mothers adopting a child below 3 months are entitled to 12 weeks of leave
Adoptive mothers are entitled to 12 weeks only when the child is below 3 years
All adoptive mothers are entitled to 12 weeks of leave irrespective of the child’s age
1.x: The Supreme Court struck down Section 60(4) of the Code on Social Security, 2020 and held that all adoptive mothers are entitled to 12 weeks of leave irrespective of the child’s age. The earlier rule limited the benefit to mothers adopting a child below 3 months.
1.tq: Direct Recall · tests the “Maternity leave for adoptive mothers” angle
n: Case: Hamsanandini Nanduri v. Union of India; Bench Justice J.B. Pardiwala and Justice R. Mahadevan (March 2026) [May 2026 · SC: 12 weeks maternity leave for all adoptive mothers]
Struck down Section 60(4) of Code on Social Security, 2020 — earlier only mothers adopting child below 3 months got 12 weeks [May 2026 · SC: 12 weeks maternity leave for all adoptive mothers]
Now all adoptive mothers get 12 weeks irrespective of child's age; violated Article 14 and Article 21 [May 2026 · SC: 12 weeks maternity leave for all adoptive mothers]

1.s: According to the Supreme Court ruling of 19 May 2026, under what condition may rabid and incurably ill stray dogs be euthanised?
o: Only after examination by a veterinarian, in line with the Animal Birth Control Rules, 2023
Immediately after being found near a school, hospital or bus station
Only after sterilisation under the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960
Only on the recommendation of an Anti-Rabies Centre in every district
1.x: The Supreme Court permitted euthanasia of rabid and incurably ill stray dogs only after veterinary examination and in accordance with the Animal Birth Control Rules, 2023. The ruling did not permit immediate removal or euthanasia merely because dogs were found near public places; sterilised dogs were not to be released at the same public places.
1.tq: Direct Recall · tests the “Ruling on euthanasia” angle
n: 19 May 2026; Bench Justices Vikram Nath, Sandeep Mehta, N.V. Anjaria [May 2026 · SC permits euthanasia of rabid and incurably ill stray dogs]
Euthanasia only after vet examination; in line with Animal Birth Control Rules, 2023 [May 2026 · SC permits euthanasia of rabid and incurably ill stray dogs]

Refused to modify 7 November 2025 order on removing stray dogs from schools, hospitals, bus stations; sterilised dogs not to be released at same public places [May 2026 · SC permits euthanasia of rabid and incurably ill stray dogs]
One ABC Centre in every district; anti-rabies medicines [May 2026 · SC permits euthanasia of rabid and incurably ill stray dogs]
Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960 [May 2026 · SC permits euthanasia of rabid and incurably ill stray dogs]

1.s: The judicial digitisation initiative ‘One Case One Data’ is designed to create which of the following?
o: A database linking only the 25 High Courts to the National Legal Services Authority
A paperless judiciary limited to Sikkim’s 32 judicial seats
A unified database linking 20,000+ taluka and district courts and 25 High Courts to the Supreme Court’s Case Information System
A network connecting 20,000+ taluka and district courts exclusively to the Supreme Court Registry’s chatbot
1.x: One Case One Data provides a unified database linking more than 20,000 taluka and district courts and 25 High Courts with the Supreme Court’s Case Information System. It is not limited to Sikkim, the High Courts alone, or the Su Sahay chatbot.

1.s: How did the Madhya Pradesh High Court characterise the Bhojshala Complex in Dhar district?
o: As the Kamal Maula Mosque, established by the Archaeological Survey of India in 1861
As a historically Saraswati Temple and centre of Sanskrit learning linked to King Bhoja of the Parmar dynasty
As a complex used exclusively for Muslim prayers on Fridays under the 2003 arrangement
As a modern Sanskrit-learning centre managed solely by the Centre and the Archaeological Survey of India
1.x: The Madhya Pradesh High Court held that the Bhojshala Complex was historically a Saraswati Temple and a centre of Sanskrit learning linked to King Bhoja of the Parmar dynasty. The name Kamal Maula Mosque is used by Muslims, while the Centre and ASI were to decide management; the complex was not characterised as exclusively a Friday-prayer site or as an ASI-established modern centre.
1.tq: Direct Recall · tests the “Historical characterisation of Bhojshala” angle

32.s: Which of the following statements about festivals in news is incorrect?
o: Nowruz is the Parsi/Persian New Year meaning “New Day” and is recognised as UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage.
Gangaur procession was held at Tripolia Bazaar in Jaipur on March 21, 2026, beginning from Janani Deodi.
Chapchar Kut is a Mizoram spring festival held after planting for jhum cultivation.
Sarhul is a Jharkhand tribal festival involving worship of the Sal tree, with Sama Maa as the deity.
32.x: The incorrect statement is the fourth option. Chapchar Kut is held after clearing for jhum cultivation, not after planting; the other three statements correctly describe Nowruz, Gangaur and Sarhul.

32.s: Under which provision was Palampet Gollalagudi in Mulugu district, Telangana, proposed to be brought under the protection of the Archaeological Survey of India?
o: The draft notification of the Ministry of Culture without reference to the AMASR Act
The establishment provision of the ASI, 1861
